newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Prudential Securities opens Brazil office.
newsitem.headline: Prudential Securities opens Brazil office.

text.p: Prudential Securities, the fourth largest U.S. brokerage house, opened a Brazil office in Sao Paulo Tuesday in a move that completes the investment bank's South America expansion plan.

"We recognize that Brazil in particular offers extraordinary opportunities and the economic growth in this country and surrounding countries continues at an extraordinarily rapid rate," said Laurence Norton, president of the firm's futures division.

The Sao Paulo office will open with 11 brokers, a number Norton said should double in the next two years. The firm also hopes to have $300 million to $400 million in assets under management by that time.
Prudential will focus on asset management in Brazil, but it will also seek to underwrite global bond and equity issues for Brazilian firms and municipalities, Norton said.
Prudential Securities, a wholly owned subsidiary of Prudential Insurance Company of America, already has South American offices in Buenos Aires, Montevideo and Santiago.

When asked why the investment bank waited to open a Brazil office last, Prudential's Latin America director Leslie Adams said: "Brazil three years ago had an economic situation much different from today. We are now very confident in Brazil."
Adams referred to the successful anti-inflation drive known as the Real Plan, which has slashed price hikes from nearly 3,000 percent to single digits over the past three years.
The plan has also brought a stable economic environment to Brazil for the first time since the 1970s. This has attracted a wave of foreign direct investment that could reach $15 billion this year.

Prudential sees Brazil as an "engine" for the investment bank's growth in Latin America. The region now accounts for $40 million, or about 10 percent of its non-U.S. revenue. Prudential forecasts that within two years, Latin America will account for 25 percent of its total non-U.S. revenue.

Prudential Securities sales last year totaled $3.2 billion, making it the fourth largest U.S. brokerage in terms of sales. It is the latest U.S. investment bank to arrive in Brazil, which has drawn dozens in the past two years.
Most recently, Morgan Stanley opened a derivatives trading desk and investment bank operation last month.
The growing presence of U.S. firms has increasingly thinned profit margins for underwriting activity in Brazil. But Prudential's Adams said the firm was not concerned about the trend.
"We might not make much on an underwriting deal but we have a large number of clients who want to invest in these issues so just being able to sell it to them justifies the transaction," he said.
